---
title: "{{PIPELINE_NAME}}"

format:
  html:
    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Layout — no TOC; navigation via top-level tabset
    page-layout: full
    smooth-scroll: true
    embed-resources: true

    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Code — single toggle in header, not per-chunk
    code-tools: true

    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Light / dark mode
    theme:
      light: [cosmo, marmot.scss]
      dark: [cyborg, marmot.scss]
    color-mode:
      toggle: true
      respect-prefers-color-scheme: true

    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Grid sizing
    grid:
      body-width: 1600px
      sidebar-width: 250px
      margin-width: 100px

    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Header (banner with title overlay, tab cleanup)
    include-in-header:
      - marmot_header.html
      - text: |
          <style>
          .cell-output-display img,
          .quarto-figure img,
          .figure img {
            max-width: 100% !important;
            height: auto !important;
          }
          </style>

    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Toolbar (top right): Find, Download, View source
    include-after-body: marmot-toolbar.html

# Execution
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
  cache: false

# Table options
df-print: paged
tbl-cap-location: top

# Cross-references
crossref:
  fig-title: "Figure"
  tbl-title: "Table"
  title-delim: ":"

lightbox: true

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fix htmlwidgets / plots in non-active tabs
include-after-body:
  text: |
    <script>
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
      document.querySelectorAll('button[data-bs-toggle="tab"]').forEach(function (btn) {
        btn.addEventListener("shown.bs.tab", function () {
          if (window.HTMLWidgets && HTMLWidgets.staticRender) {
            HTMLWidgets.staticRender();
          }
          window.dispatchEvent(new Event("resize"));
        });
      });
    });
    </script>

```{r input_settings}
## 🔧 File paths
fp <- "path/to/your/FCS_files/"      # Folder with all FCS files
md_fp <- "path/to/your/FCS_files/MARMOT_Metadata.xlsx"      # Full path to metadata Excel file
## 🧪 Preprocessing
downsampleTo <- 10000  # Cells to take from each FCS file, for a quick first look. NULL = use every cell

## 🔍 Clustering
clusteringMethodToUse <- "FlowSOM"   # One of: "MfastPG", "Mphenograph", "Mparc", "Rphenograph", "PARC", "FlowSOM"
markersToClusterBy <- "all"       # One of: "all", "type", "state"
kValuesIWant <- c(20, 40, 60)
knn <- 20          # Must be in kValuesIWant

## 📉 Dimension Reduction
dimRedMethodToUse <- "UMAP"   # One of: "TSNE", "UMAP", "Mpacmap", "pacmap"
markersToDimRedBy <- "type"   # One of: "all", "type", "state"

## 🧼 QC
runQC <- "PeacoQC"      # One of: "FlowAI", "PeacoQC", or "None" to skip
useQC <- FALSE            # Whether to keep only QC-passed cells

## 💾 Output
RDataFolder <- NULL # Use existing results (skip re-analysis)
excludeTheseSamples <- NULL           # e.g. c("Sample_001", "Sample_026"), or NULL
gimmePDFs <- FALSE
greyscalePlots <- FALSE
quantileNormaliseAll <- FALSE

## 🧠 Resources
nCores <- 4
ramPerCore <- 6

## 🎨 Aesthetics
viridisColour <- "lapaz"   # Viridis, Scico, RColorBrewer Diverging, or Fun (Marmot, Swiss, Lucky)
figureDPI <- 120           # Resolution of the report's figures: higher is sharper, but the report gets bigger

## 🌉 scGate (optional)
runScGate <- FALSE    # Set TRUE to run scGate marker-pair gating (requires scGate, UCell, Seurat)

## 🧪 Batch correction (optional)
batchColumn <- NULL   # File Data column naming each sample's batch, e.g. "Batch". Blank = no batch correction

## 📁 Results directory (set by marmot(); leave NULL for manual runs)
resultsDir <- NULL

## Done editing? Knit away!
```

```{r setup_palettes, include = FALSE}
viridis_palettes <- c("magma", "inferno", "plasma", "viridis", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo")
scico_palettes   <- c("bam", "berlin", "brocO", "corkO", "lapaz", "lisbon", "romaO", "vikO")
fun_palettes <- list(
  Marmot = c("#4a3728", "#6b5344", "#8c7a6b", "#a89888", "#bfb5a8", "#d4ccc4", "#9e9e9e", "#787878"),
  Swiss  = c("#ffffff", "#ffe5e5", "#ffb3b3", "#ff6666", "#ff1a1a", "#cc0000", "#990000")
)

get_palette_colours <- function(palette, n = 64) {
  if (palette %in% viridis_palettes) {
    viridis::viridis(n, option = palette)
  } else if (palette %in% scico_palettes) {
    scico::scico(n, palette = palette)
  } else if (palette == "Lucky") {
    colorRampPalette(sample(grDevices::colors(distinct = TRUE), 3))(n)
  } else if (palette %in% names(fun_palettes)) {
    colorRampPalette(fun_palettes[[palette]])(n)
  } else {
    # Diverging (RColorBrewer)
    colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, palette))(n)
  }
}
```

```{r setup_helpers, include = FALSE}
# Parse "CellType: Marker1 Marker2" entries from the Marker Pairs column
parse_marker_pairs <- function(smd) {
  if (!"Marker Pairs" %in% colnames(smd)) return(NULL)
  pairs <- smd[["Marker Pairs"]][!is.na(smd[["Marker Pairs"]])]
  if (length(pairs) == 0) return(NULL)
  types <- unique(gsub("\\:.*", "", pairs))
  names(pairs) <- gsub("\\:.*", "", pairs)
  models <- lapply(types, function(tp) {
    entry <- pairs[names(pairs) == tp][[1]]
    markers <- strsplit(entry, "\\:\\s*")[[1]][[2]]
    strsplit(markers, "\\s+")[[1]]
  })
  names(models) <- types
  list(pairs = unname(pairs), types = types, models = models)
}

# Build coloursList entries for scGate results
setup_scgate_colours <- function(gated_cells, model_names, palette) {
  cols <- list()
  gate_pal <- palette[seq_along(gated_cells)]
  names(gate_pal) <- gated_cells
  cols[["Gated_Cells"]] <- gate_pal
  for (x in model_names) {
    y <- gsub(" |-", "", x)
    cols[[paste0("is_", y)]] <- setNames("steelblue", x)
  }
  cols
}

# Rewrite ComplexHeatmap top-annotation colours from coloursList. Four slots
# need to be poked per condition because ComplexHeatmap caches color_mapping
# both on the anno_list slot and inside the draw closure's var_env.
apply_anno_colours <- function(pDH, conditions, coloursList) {
  for (con in conditions) {
    cm <- pDH@top_annotation@anno_list[[con]]@color_mapping
    new_cols <- coloursList[[con]][match(names(cm@colors), names(coloursList[[con]]))]
    pDH@top_annotation@anno_list[[con]]@color_mapping@colors <- new_cols
    pDH@top_annotation@anno_list[[con]]@color_mapping@full_col <- new_cols
    pDH@top_annotation@anno_list[[con]]@fun@var_env[["color_mapping"]]@colors <- new_cols
    pDH@top_annotation@anno_list[[con]]@fun@var_env[["color_mapping"]]@full_col <- new_cols
  }
  pDH
}

# Build inputs for the `Heatmaps of DA Clusters` chunk. This replaces the
# old `function for custom heatmap` chunk that leaked x / z / lgd_aes into
# the global env via CATALYST internals.
build_da_heatmap_inputs <- function(sce, k, assay = "exprs",
                                    fun = "median", q = 0.01) {
  x <- sce[unique(CATALYST:::.get_features(sce, NULL)), ]
  CATALYST:::.check_k(x, k)
  x$cluster_id <- cluster_ids(x, k)

  # "first" scale path: scale the assay, then aggregate.
  z_assay <- CATALYST:::.scale_exprs(assay(x, assay), 1, q)
  assay(x, assay, FALSE) <- z_assay
  z <- CATALYST:::.agg(x, "cluster_id", fun, assay)
  z <- t(z)

  qs <- round(quantile(z, c(0.01, 0.99)) * 5) / 5
  lgd_aes <- list(
    at = seq(qs[1], qs[2], 0.2),
    title_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.8)
  )

  list(x = x, z = z, lgd_aes = lgd_aes)
}

# The start of a PDF file name, made from the name of a group of clusters:
# "Contrast 1: A over B Up" becomes "Contrast_1_A_over_B_Up".
pdf_name_stem <- function(name) {
  cx <- name |> gsub(pattern = ": .*", replacement = "", x = _) |> gsub(pattern = "Contrast ", replacement = "Contrast_", x = _) |> gsub(pattern = "\\/", replacement = "", x = _)
  sx <- name |> gsub(pattern = ".*\\: ", replacement = "", x = _) |> gsub(pattern = " ", replacement = "_", x = _) |> gsub(pattern = "\\/", replacement = "", x = _)
  paste0(cx, "_", sx)
}
```

```{r setup_embedding_plot}
# Draws one embedding plot. The default point size, `dr_point_size`, is set
# from the number of plotted cells just before the report is drawn. The look
# follows the manuscript figures: no axes, a fixed aspect ratio, a black halo
# around the cells, and two arrows in the corner naming the axes
# (MARMOT::dr_corner_arrows()).
dr_legend_dot <- 5   # size of the dots in every map legend
plotUMAPNice <- function(
  df = umapDF,
  colour_by = "condition",
  show_density = FALSE,
  size = dr_point_size,
  alpha = 1,
  text_size = 12,
  facet_by = NULL,
  show_grids = FALSE,
  name = "Normalised\nExpression\n",
  show_cluster_labels = FALSE,
  cluster_labels = "cluster_id",
  border = TRUE,
  border_size = 2,
  border_density = 1,
  border_colour = "black"
) {
  gp <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[["x"]], y = .data[["y"]], colour = .data[[colour_by]]))

  # Density overlay
  if (show_density) {
    gp <- gp +
      geom_density_2d(
        data = df[, c("x", "y")],
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        colour = "lightgrey",
        size = 0.5,
        bins = 20,
        alpha = 0.8
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(
        xlim = range(df$x, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-1, 1),
        ylim = range(df$y, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-1, 1)
      )
  }

  if (border && nrow(df) > 10) {
    kde <- MASS::kde2d(df[["x"]], df[["y"]], n = 100L)
    ix  <- pmax(1L, pmin(findInterval(df[["x"]], kde$x), length(kde$x)))
    iy  <- pmax(1L, pmin(findInterval(df[["y"]], kde$y), length(kde$y)))
    cell_density <- kde$z[cbind(ix, iy)]
    border_df <- df[cell_density <= quantile(cell_density, border_density), ]
    # As SCpubr draws it: points at half size, the halo twice that, solid colours
    eff_size <- size / 2
    gp <- gp +
      geom_point(data = border_df, size = eff_size * border_size,
                 colour = border_colour, show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_point(colour = "grey75", size = eff_size, show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_point(size = eff_size)
  } else {
    gp <- gp + geom_point(size = size, alpha = alpha, shape = 16)
  }

  gp <- gp +
    labs(title = if (colour_by %in% useMarkers) MARMOT::marker_label(colour_by, markerDisplay) else MARMOT::greek_label(colour_by)) +
    MARMOT::dr_corner_arrows(df[, c("x", "y")], MARMOT::dr_axis_names(dimRedMethodToUse)) +
    theme_prism() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
    )

  # Guides: big legend dots for groups
  if (!colour_by %in% useMarkers) {
    gp <- gp + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = dr_legend_dot, alpha = 1)))
  }

  # Cluster label overlays
  if (show_cluster_labels) {
    label_coords <- data.frame(
      df |>
        dplyr::group_by(.data[[cluster_labels]]) |>
        dplyr::summarise(x = median(x), y = median(y)))
    # Labels with a Greek letter are drawn with plotmath; others as they are
    parse_labels <- is.expression(MARMOT::greek_label(label_coords[[cluster_labels]]))
    label_coords$label_text <- if (parse_labels) MARMOT::greek_parse_text(label_coords[[cluster_labels]]) else as.character(label_coords[[cluster_labels]])
    if (colour_by %in% useMarkers) {
      label_coords[[colour_by]] <- lapply(label_coords[[cluster_labels]], function(level) {
        mean(df[[colour_by]][df[[cluster_labels]] == level])
      }) |> unlist()
      gp <- gp + geom_label_repel(data = label_coords, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label_text, fill = .data[[colour_by]]), parse = parse_labels, colour = "black", show.legend = FALSE)
    } else {
      gp <- gp + geom_label_repel(data = label_coords, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label_text, fill = .data[[cluster_labels]]), parse = parse_labels, colour = "black", show.legend = FALSE)
    }
  }

  if (!show_grids) {
    gp <- gp +
      theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  }

  # Gradient or manual colour scale
  if (colour_by %in% useMarkers) {
    gp <- gp + scale_colour_gradientn(name, colours = get_palette_colours(viridisColour))
    gp <- gp + scale_fill_gradientn(name, colours = get_palette_colours(viridisColour))
  } else {
    gp <- gp + scale_colour_manual(values = coloursList[[colour_by]], labels = MARMOT::greek_label)
    gp <- gp + scale_fill_manual(values = coloursList[[colour_by]], labels = MARMOT::greek_label)
  }

  # Faceting
  if (!is.null(facet_by)) {
    gp <- gp + facet_wrap(facets = as.formula(paste("~", facet_by)), labeller = MARMOT::label_greek)
  }

  return(gp)
}
```

<!-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     PART 3: RELOAD. Only does anything when RDataFolder points at saved results.
     The two chunks after it need to know whether results were reloaded.
     ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

```{r reload_results, include = FALSE, results = 'asis'}

if (!is.null(RDataFolder)) {
  # Auto-resolve: if user pointed to the top-level Results_Files dir, descend into R_files/
  h5ad_path <- file.path(RDataFolder, "marmot_results.h5ad")
  if (!file.exists(h5ad_path) &&
       file.exists(file.path(RDataFolder, "R_files", "marmot_results.h5ad"))) {
    RDataFolder <- file.path(RDataFolder, "R_files")
    h5ad_path <- file.path(RDataFolder, "marmot_results.h5ad")
    message("ℹ️ Auto-resolved RDataFolder to: ", RDataFolder)
  }
  if (!file.exists(h5ad_path)) {
    stop("No h5ad data found in ", RDataFolder,
         ". Please re-run the pipeline to generate h5ad output.")
  }
  message(glue::glue("🔁 Loading results from h5ad: {h5ad_path}"))
  MARMOT::load_h5ad_to_env(h5ad_path, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  # The sample table comes back with row names ("1", "2", ...), which diffcyt
  # refuses; a fresh run has none, so remove them
  rownames(metadata(sce)$experiment_info) <- NULL
  # Load DA/DS result objects (S4 structures that can't survive h5ad)
  da_ds_path <- file.path(RDataFolder, "da_ds_results.qs2")
  if (file.exists(da_ds_path)) {
    da_ds <- qs2::qs_read(da_ds_path, nthreads = nCores)
    for (nm in names(da_ds)) {
      if (!is.null(da_ds[[nm]])) assign(nm, da_ds[[nm]], envir = .GlobalEnv)
    }
    # sceDS was saved without its expression data: give it back from `sce`
    if (exists("sceDS")) sceDS <- MARMOT::restore_slim_sce(sceDS, sce)
    message("Loaded (qs2): da_ds_results.qs2")
  }

  # Reconstruct panel from rowData(sce) — the analysis_panel_cofactors chunk is skipped on reload
  rd <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(sce))
  panel <- data.frame(
    fcs_colname  = rownames(rd),
    marker_name  = if ("marker_name" %in% names(rd)) rd$marker_name else rownames(rd),
    antigen      = if ("marker_name" %in% names(rd)) rd$marker_name else rownames(rd),
    marker_class = if ("marker_class" %in% names(rd)) rd$marker_class else "none",
    use_channel  = TRUE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Inject md columns into colData — prepData did this on fresh run via
  # md_cols = list(factors = conditions), but h5ad doesn't preserve the merge.
  cd <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce))
  md_reload <- as.data.frame(md)
  md_extra_cols <- setdiff(names(md_reload), c("file_name", names(cd)))
  if (length(md_extra_cols) > 0) {
    lookup <- md_reload[, c("sample_id", md_extra_cols), drop = FALSE]
    matched <- lookup[match(cd$sample_id, lookup$sample_id), md_extra_cols, drop = FALSE]
    rownames(matched) <- rownames(cd)
    for (col in md_extra_cols) {
      SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)[[col]] <- matched[[col]]
    }
    message("ℹ️  Injected md columns into colData: ", paste(md_extra_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
}
```

```{r setup_derived_settings, include = FALSE}
# Pick the merge method depending on clustering backend
mergeBy <- dplyr::case_when(
  clusteringMethodToUse %in% c("Rphenograph", "Mphenograph", "MfastPG") ~ "k",
  clusteringMethodToUse %in% c("PARC", "Mparc") ~ "p",
  clusteringMethodToUse == "FlowSOM" ~ "meta",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_  # temp placeholder
)
if (is.na(mergeBy)) stop("Unsupported clustering method: ", clusteringMethodToUse)

# Figure resolution for every figure from here on
if (!is.numeric(figureDPI) || length(figureDPI) != 1 || is.na(figureDPI) || figureDPI < 50 || figureDPI > 600) {
  stop("Oops! figureDPI should be a number between 50 and 600 (120 is a good start). ",
       "Please check it in the Pipeline Settings sheet.", call. = FALSE)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = figureDPI)

# Warnings found during the analysis, shown together in the Overview tab
overviewWarnings <- character()

# Heatmap colour palette
hmPalToUse <- if (greyscalePlots) {
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Greys")
} else {
  rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "RdBu"))
}
```

```{r save_folders, results = "hide"}

# Create Results root directory if not resuming from saved RData
if (is.null(RDataFolder)) {
  if (is.null(resultsDir)) {
    # Manual run (RStudio) — create results dir with timestamp
    resultsDir <- file.path(fp, paste0("Results_Files_", timeRun))
    dir.create(resultsDir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  }

  rFilesDir <- file.path(resultsDir, "R_files")
  dir.create(rFilesDir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
}

# When reloading, RDataFolder points to R_files/ — go up one level for sibling dirs
reloadResultsDir <- if (!is.null(RDataFolder)) dirname(RDataFolder) else NULL

# PDFs
if (gimmePDFs) {
  pdfDir <- if (is.null(RDataFolder)) {
    file.path(resultsDir, "PDF_figures")
  } else {
    file.path(reloadResultsDir, "PDF_figures")
  }
  dir.create(pdfDir, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

# Excel outputs
excelDir <- if (is.null(RDataFolder)) {
  file.path(resultsDir, "Excel_Files")
} else {
  file.path(reloadResultsDir, "Excel_Files")
}
dir.create(excelDir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r analysis_metadata, results = "hide"}

# ── Initialise run log (marmot_run_log.json) ──────────────────────────────
# Shape-only diagnostics for remote debugging. Never writes cell-level values
# or identifying labels. Written progressively so mid-pipeline crashes still
# leave a useful file.
# It sits in the R_files folder (see the `save_folders` chunk). A reload keeps
# its own log beside the original, so the original run's log is never replaced.
log_path <- if (!is.null(RDataFolder)) {
  file.path(RDataFolder, "marmot_run_log_reload.json")
} else {
  file.path(rFilesDir, "marmot_run_log.json")
}
.diag_get <- function(name, default = NA) {
  if (exists(name, envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) {
    v <- get(name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    if (is.null(v)) default else v
  } else default
}
MARMOT::run_log_start(log_path, settings = list(
  clusteringMethodToUse = as.character(.diag_get("clusteringMethodToUse")),
  markersToClusterBy    = as.character(.diag_get("markersToClusterBy")),
  kValuesIWant          = as.character(.diag_get("kValuesIWant")),
  knn                   = .diag_get("knn"),
  dimRedMethodToUse     = as.character(.diag_get("dimRedMethodToUse")),
  markersToDimRedBy     = as.character(.diag_get("markersToDimRedBy")),
  runQC                 = as.character(.diag_get("runQC")),
  useQC                 = isTRUE(.diag_get("useQC", FALSE)),
  runScGate             = isTRUE(.diag_get("runScGate", FALSE)),
  downsampleTo          = .diag_get("downsampleTo", NA),
  quantileNormaliseAll  = isTRUE(.diag_get("quantileNormaliseAll", FALSE)),
  nCores                = .diag_get("nCores"),
  ramPerCore            = .diag_get("ramPerCore"),
  reload                = !is.null(RDataFolder)
))

# Load metadata
md  <- readxl::read_xlsx(md_fp, sheet = "File Data")
smd <- readxl::read_xlsx(md_fp, sheet = "Study Data")

# Paths
fcsDir <- fp

# Order sample IDs naturally
md <- md[gtools::mixedorder(md$sample_id), ]
md$sample_id <- factor(md$sample_id, levels = md$sample_id)

# Apply condition ordering if available
conditionOrder <- smd$`Conditions Order` |> na.omit()

nameNotes <- character()   # names spelt differently and lined up, for the Overview

# Samples to exclude may be spelt differently from File Data's sample IDs too.
# One that matches nothing is not excluded, and the Overview says so.
if (!is.null(excludeTheseSamples)) {
  sampleExcludeMatch <- MARMOT::match_names(excludeTheseSamples, as.character(md$sample_id))
  nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, MARMOT::describe_name_matches(sampleExcludeMatch$notes, "sample to exclude", "'File Data'"))
  excludeTheseSamples <- stats::na.omit(sampleExcludeMatch$matched)
  if (!length(excludeTheseSamples)) excludeTheseSamples <- NULL
}

# Every sample needs a condition, spelt exactly as in 'Conditions Order'.
# Otherwise its cells end up with no condition, and the run stops much later
# with a puzzling error. (Samples about to be excluded are not checked.)
condsInUse <- md$condition[!md$sample_id %in% excludeTheseSamples]
if (anyNA(condsInUse)) {
  stop("❌ Some samples in 'File Data' have no condition: ",
       paste(md$sample_id[is.na(md$condition) & !md$sample_id %in% excludeTheseSamples], collapse = ", "),
       ". Please fill in their condition.")
}
if (length(conditionOrder) > 0) {
  # A condition spelt differently ("control", "Control ", "Treated-A") counts
  # as the one in 'Conditions Order', whose spelling is used from here on
  condMatch <- MARMOT::match_names(unique(as.character(condsInUse)), conditionOrder)
  notInOrder <- condMatch$notes$wanted[condMatch$notes$how == "missing"]
  if (length(notInOrder)) {
    quoteCond <- function(x) paste0("'", x, "'")
    stop("❌ These conditions in 'File Data' are missing from 'Conditions Order' on the 'Study Data' sheet: ",
         paste(quoteCond(notInOrder), collapse = ", "), ". 'Conditions Order' has: ",
         paste(quoteCond(conditionOrder), collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
  md$condition <- condMatch$matched[match(as.character(md$condition), unique(as.character(condsInUse)))] |>
    dplyr::coalesce(as.character(md$condition))   # excluded samples keep theirs
  nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, MARMOT::describe_name_matches(condMatch$notes, "condition", "'Conditions Order'"))
}

if (length(conditionOrder) > 0) {
  md$condition <- factor(md$condition, levels = conditionOrder)
} else {
  md$condition <- as.factor(md$condition)
}

# Extract marker names
useMarkers <- smd[[colnames(smd)[grep("include|cluster", colnames(smd))]]]
useMarkers <- useMarkers[!is.na(useMarkers)]
names(useMarkers) <- gsub("-|\\ |\\/", "_", useMarkers)

# Extract marker type vector (used downstream for marker_class and conditional sections)
# Named vector: names = marker names, values = "type"/"state"
# Named lookup prevents ifelse recycling when param_df has extra scatter/time channels
mt_mask <- !is.na(smd$`Marker Type`)
include_col <- colnames(smd)[grep("include|cluster", colnames(smd))]
# "Type", "STATE " and the like all count: only "type" and "state" are used below
markerType <- setNames(tolower(trimws(smd$`Marker Type`[mt_mask])), smd[[include_col]][mt_mask])

# Define feature type from marker type
featureType <- if ("Marker Type" %in% names(smd)) {
  types <- na.omit(smd$`Marker Type`)
  if ("type" %in% types) "type" else NULL
} else {
  warning("Metadata has no 'Marker Type' column \u2014 all markers will be used for clustering and DR.")
  NULL
}

# Homogeneous panel: missing one of the two marker classes (type or state).
# Reuses the idiom already used at the marker-pair / heatmap chunks later.
# When TRUE, clustering and DR override markersToClusterBy / markersToDimRedBy
# and run on every marker in the panel — the type/state distinction is
# meaningless here. Defined in the always-running analysis_metadata chunk so it
# is available on both fresh and reload paths.
homogeneousPanel <- !(("type" %in% markerType) && ("state" %in% markerType))
if (homogeneousPanel) {
  message(sprintf(
    "\u2139\ufe0f  Panel is homogeneous \u2014 clustering and DR will run on all %d markers, ignoring markersToClusterBy/markersToDimRedBy.",
    length(markerType)
  ))
}

# Markers to exclude
removeMarkers <- na.omit(smd$`Markers to exclude completely`)

# Cofactors: each one belongs to the marker on the same row
cfToUse <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(smd$`Cofactors for markers to use`[!is.na(smd[[include_col]])]))
if (anyNA(cfToUse)) {
  stop("❌ Every marker in '", include_col, "' needs a cofactor (a number) on the same row in ",
       "'Cofactors for markers to use'. Please check: ",
       paste(useMarkers[is.na(cfToUse)], collapse = ", "))
}

# Display names: how each marker is named in figures (for example with Greek
# letters). Optional; matching always uses the marker's own name.
markerDisplay <- if ("Display names for markers" %in% names(smd)) {
  d <- trimws(as.character(smd$`Display names for markers`[!is.na(smd[[include_col]])]))
  stats::setNames(d, useMarkers)[!is.na(d) & nzchar(d)]
} else NULL

# Contrasts
# Each entry reads "A over B"; "vs", "versus" and "v" are read as "over" too.
# Blank entries, and a bare " over " left by empty dropdowns, are skipped;
# anything else that cannot be read as "A over B" stops the run.
contrastSep <- "(?i)(?= (over|versus|vs\\.?|v\\.?) )"
contrastsToTest <- na.omit(smd$`Conditions To Test`)
contrastsToTest <- gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(contrastsToTest))
contrastsToTest <- contrastsToTest[!grepl("(?i)^(over|versus|vs\\.?|v\\.?)?$", contrastsToTest, perl = TRUE)]
unreadable <- !grepl("(?i). (over|versus|vs\\.?|v\\.?) .", contrastsToTest, perl = TRUE)
if (any(unreadable)) {
  stop("❌ Each entry in 'Conditions To Test' needs to read 'A over B', for example 'KO over WT'. ",
       "Please check: ", paste0("'", contrastsToTest[unreadable], "'", collapse = ", "))
}
# Each side may be spelt differently from the conditions ("treated over control");
# it is rewritten with the conditions' own spelling. A contrast that still does
# not match is left as typed (with "over"), and the DA/DS step says so clearly.
contrastCondNames <- if (length(conditionOrder)) conditionOrder else unique(as.character(md$condition))
for (i in seq_along(contrastsToTest)) {
  ctr <- contrastsToTest[[i]]
  cuts <- gregexpr(contrastSep, ctr, perl = TRUE)[[1]]
  sepLen <- attr(cuts, "capture.length")[, 1] + 2
  for (j in seq_along(cuts)) {
    m <- MARMOT::match_names(c(substr(ctr, 1, cuts[j] - 1), substr(ctr, cuts[j] + sepLen[j], nchar(ctr))), contrastCondNames)
    if (!anyNA(m$matched) && m$matched[1] != m$matched[2]) {
      contrastsToTest[[i]] <- paste(m$matched[1], "over", m$matched[2])
      break
    }
  }
  if (contrastsToTest[[i]] == ctr && !grepl("(?i) over ", ctr, perl = TRUE)) {
    contrastsToTest[[i]] <- sub("(?i) (versus|vs\\.?|v\\.?) ", " over ", ctr, perl = TRUE)
  }
  if (contrastsToTest[[i]] != ctr) {
    nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, sprintf("The contrast '%s' was read as '%s'.", ctr, contrastsToTest[[i]]))
  }
}
contrastsToTest <- as.character(contrastsToTest)
contrastsToTestS <- paste(contrastsToTest, collapse = ",")
cTTForPlots <- contrastsToTest

# Subsampling settings: how many cells per sample to show in UMAPs etc., given
# per condition on the same row as its entry in 'Conditions Order'. An entry is
# a number or simple arithmetic such as 12000/6. Leave the whole column blank
# to show every cell.
raw_subsamp <- as.character(smd$`Cells per condition in UMAPs etc.`[!is.na(smd$`Conditions Order`)])
if (all(is.na(raw_subsamp))) {
  drCellPerCondition <- NULL
} else {
  # Only numbers and arithmetic are accepted, since the entry is evaluated as R code
  notArithmetic <- is.na(raw_subsamp) | !grepl("^[0-9eE+*/(). -]+$", raw_subsamp)
  if (any(notArithmetic)) {
    stop("❌ 'Cells per condition in UMAPs etc.' needs, for every condition, the number of cells to show ",
         "from each of its samples: a number, or simple arithmetic such as 10000/3 (no thousands separators). ",
         "Or leave the whole column blank to show every cell. ",
         "Please check: ", paste(conditionOrder[notArithmetic], collapse = ", "))
  }
  drCellPerCondition <- setNames(
    vapply(raw_subsamp, function(expr) as.numeric(eval(parse(text = expr))), numeric(1)),
    conditionOrder
  )
}

# Identify all condition columns
# Hyphens in extra column names become dots, in File Data too, so the two agree
names(md) <- gsub("-", ".", names(md))
conditions <- c("condition", setdiff(names(md), c("file_name", "sample_id", "condition")))

# Exclude samples if specified
if (!is.null(excludeTheseSamples)) {
  md <- md[!md$sample_id %in% excludeTheseSamples, ]
}

# Sort again by condition
md <- md[order(md$condition), ]
md$sample_id  <- factor(md$sample_id, levels = md$sample_id)

# Batch correction (only when batchColumn names a File Data column). The
# design is checked here, before any heavy work: a design that cannot work
# stops the run in plain words (see ?MARMOT::check_batch_design).
useBatch <- !is.null(batchColumn) && nzchar(trimws(batchColumn))
batchNotes <- character()
if (useBatch) {
  batchMatch <- MARMOT::match_names(gsub("-", ".", batchColumn), setdiff(names(md), c("file_name", "sample_id", "condition")))
  if (is.na(batchMatch$matched)) {
    stop("❌ The batchColumn setting names '", batchColumn, "', but the File Data sheet has no such column. ",
         "Its columns are: ", paste(names(md), collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
  nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, MARMOT::describe_name_matches(batchMatch$notes, "batch column", "'File Data'"))
  batchColumn <- batchMatch$matched
  if (!clusteringMethodToUse %in% c("MfastPG", "Mphenograph", "Mparc", "PARC", "Rphenograph")) {
    stop("❌ Batch correction works with the graph clustering methods (MfastPG, Mphenograph, Mparc, ",
         "PARC, Rphenograph), not with ", clusteringMethodToUse, ". Choose one of those, or leave batchColumn blank.")
  }
  if (!requireNamespace("harmony", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("❌ Batch correction needs the harmony package. Install it with install.packages(\"harmony\"), ",
         "or leave batchColumn blank.")
  }
  batchNotes <- MARMOT::check_batch_design(md[[batchColumn]], md$condition, md$sample_id, batchColumn)
}

# ── Diagnostic: metadata shape (counts only, no labels) ───────────────────
MARMOT::run_log_record(log_path, "data_shape", list(
  n_samples    = nrow(md),
  n_conditions = nlevels(md$condition),
  n_contrasts  = length(na.omit(smd$`Conditions To Test`)),
  n_markers_requested = length(useMarkers),
  homogeneous_panel   = isTRUE(homogeneousPanel)
))
MARMOT::run_log_checkpoint(log_path, "analysis_metadata")
```


```{r analysis_condition_colours, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

# Collect all unique factor levels from the specified metadata columns
allConditionLevels <- unlist(lapply(conditions, \(x) levels(factor(md[[x]]))), use.names = FALSE)

# Assign colours to each unique level using a palette combo (expand as needed)
palettePool <- c(
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Set1"),
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"),
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"),
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set3")
)
if (length(allConditionLevels) > length(palettePool)) {
  palettePool <- colorRampPalette(palettePool)(length(allConditionLevels))
}

allConditionLevelColours <- setNames(palettePool[seq_along(allConditionLevels)], allConditionLevels)

# Create named list of colours per condition
coloursList <- setNames(
  lapply(conditions, \(x) {
    levels <- levels(factor(md[[x]]))
    allConditionLevelColours[levels]
  }),
  conditions
)

# Assign sample-level colours
sampleCols <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))(length(levels(md$sample_id))),
  levels(md$sample_id)
)

# Assign condition-level colours
conditionCols <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set1"))(length(levels(md$condition))),
  levels(md$condition)
)
```

```{r analysis_fcs_scan, include = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

message("📥 Scanning FCS files...")

# Match File Data's file names to the files on disk. A name spelt differently
# ("sample_01.FCS" for "Sample-01.fcs") still finds its file, and the Overview
# says so. Extra files in fcsDir are ignored; a name with no file is fatal.
disk_files <- list.files(fcsDir, pattern = "\\.fcs$", full.names = FALSE, ignore.case = TRUE)
fileMatch <- MARMOT::match_names(md$file_name, disk_files)
missing <- fileMatch$notes$wanted[fileMatch$notes$how == "missing"]
if (length(missing)) {
  stop("FCS files listed in metadata not found in ", fcsDir, ":\n  ",
       paste(missing, collapse = "\n  "))
}
nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, MARMOT::describe_name_matches(fileMatch$notes, "file", "the FCS folder"))
fcs_files <- file.path(fcsDir, fileMatch$matched)   # the files as they are on disk
fcs_names <- md$file_name                            # ... and as File Data names them

# ── Header scan — get cell counts without loading data ────────────────────────
fcs_headers <- sapply(fcs_files, function(f) {
  hdr <- flowCore::read.FCSheader(f)
  c(tot = as.numeric(hdr[[1]]["$TOT"]),
    par = as.numeric(hdr[[1]]["$PAR"]))
})
originalCellCounts <- setNames(fcs_headers["tot", ], fcs_names)
total_cells_raw    <- sum(originalCellCounts)
n_params           <- fcs_headers["par", 1]
n_samples          <- length(fcs_files)

# ── Compute RAM budget and per-sample cap ─────────────────────────────────────
sys_ram_bytes <- tryCatch({
  os <- Sys.info()[["sysname"]]
  if (os == "Darwin") {
    as.numeric(system("sysctl -n hw.memsize", intern = TRUE))
  } else if (os == "Linux") {
    as.numeric(system("awk '/MemTotal/{print $2 * 1024}' /proc/meminfo", intern = TRUE))
  } else {
    NA_real_   # Windows: cross-version RAM probing is unreliable (wmic deprecated,
               # PowerShell availability varies); trust user's ramPerCore * nCores.
  }
}, error = function(e) NA_real_)
sys_ram_gb <- if (!is.na(sys_ram_bytes)) sys_ram_bytes / 1024^3 else Inf

if (is.na(sys_ram_bytes) && Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Windows") {
  warning(
    "⚠️  Could not detect system RAM on this Windows machine. ",
    "Falling back to your declared budget (ramPerCore × nCores = ",
    sprintf("%.0f GB", ramPerCore * nCores), "). ",
    "If that exceeds the RAM actually available, the pipeline may run out of ",
    "memory and crash. Double-check ramPerCore and nCores against your machine's ",
    "specs before continuing.",
    call. = FALSE, immediate. = TRUE
  )
}

# Available RAM: lower of system RAM and user-declared budget
user_budget_gb     <- ramPerCore * nCores
available_gb       <- min(sys_ram_gb, user_budget_gb)
pipeline_budget_gb <- available_gb * 0.6   # 60% for pipeline, 40% for OS/R/Quarto
peak_multiplier    <- 2.5                  # measured 2.2× on real data; 2.5× for safety
bytes_per_cell     <- n_params * 8

max_total_cells <- floor((pipeline_budget_gb * 1024^3) / (bytes_per_cell * peak_multiplier))
per_sample_cap  <- floor(max_total_cells / n_samples)
needs_cap       <- total_cells_raw > max_total_cells

message(sprintf("📊 Dataset: %s cells × %d params across %d samples",
                format(total_cells_raw, big.mark = ","), n_params, n_samples))
message(sprintf("📊 RAM: %s system, %.0f GB user budget, %.1f GB pipeline budget (60%%)",
                if (is.finite(sys_ram_gb)) sprintf("%.0f GB", sys_ram_gb) else "unknown",
                user_budget_gb, pipeline_budget_gb))

if (needs_cap) {
  message(sprintf(
    paste0("⚠️  Dataset has %s cells but this machine can safely hold %s. ",
           "Capping to %s cells per sample (%s total)."),
    format(total_cells_raw, big.mark = ","),
    format(max_total_cells, big.mark = ","),
    format(per_sample_cap, big.mark = ","),
    format(per_sample_cap * n_samples, big.mark = ",")))
} else {
  message(sprintf("📊 Dataset fits in RAM budget (%s cells < %s max)",
                  format(total_cells_raw, big.mark = ","),
                  format(max_total_cells, big.mark = ",")))
}
```

```{r analysis_memory_cap_notice, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}
if (needs_cap) {
  overviewWarnings <- c(overviewWarnings, sprintf(
    paste0("::: {.callout-warning title='RAM Cap Applied'}\n",
           "Your dataset has **%s cells** across %d samples, but this machine ",
           "can safely hold **%s cells** in memory (%.0f GB system RAM, ",
           "%.1f GB pipeline budget at 60%%).\n\n",
           "Each sample has been capped to **%s cells**. QC ran on the full dataset. ",
           "Clustering, dimensionality reduction, and all downstream analysis use the capped data. ",
           "To use more cells, run on a machine with more RAM or increase `ramPerCore`.\n",
           ":::\n"),
    format(total_cells_raw, big.mark = ","), n_samples,
    format(max_total_cells, big.mark = ","),
    sys_ram_gb, pipeline_budget_gb,
    format(per_sample_cap, big.mark = ",")))
}
```

```{r analysis_downsample_notice, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}
           "This run took at most **%s cells** from each FCS file ",
```

```{r analysis_panel_cofactors, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

# Line the files up. Exports from different days or datasets may spell a
# marker differently ("IL7R", "Il7R", "IL-7R"), order the channels differently,
# or put a marker on another channel. Every file's header is read, and its
# channels are matched to the first file's, ignoring capitals, spaces,
# hyphens and underscores; markers in the sheet take the sheet's spelling.
# Each file is lined up as it is read (see analysis_qc_* and analysis_fcs_load),
# and the report's Overview says what was done.
fcsLineup <- MARMOT::plan_fcs_lineup(fcs_files, sheet_markers = useMarkers)
if (nrow(fcsLineup$missing)) {
  stop("❌ These markers in '", include_col, "' are missing from some FCS files:\n  ",
       paste0(fcsLineup$missing$marker, ": not in ", fcsLineup$missing$files, collapse = "\n  "),
       "\nEvery file needs every marker you analyse.")
}
nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, fcsLineup$notes)   # everything lined up, for the Overview (see the end of this chunk)
MARMOT::run_log_record(log_path, "fcs_lineup", list(notes = as.list(fcsLineup$notes)))

# The panel, from the lined-up channels (just the names, not the data)
param_df <- data.frame(name = fcsLineup$reference$channel, desc = fcsLineup$reference$marker) |>
  dplyr::mutate(desc = ifelse(is.na(desc), name, desc))

# 'Markers to exclude completely' may be spelt differently from the files too
markerExcludeMatch <- MARMOT::match_names(removeMarkers, param_df$desc)
nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, MARMOT::describe_name_matches(
  markerExcludeMatch$notes[markerExcludeMatch$notes$how != "missing", ], "marker to exclude", "the FCS files"))
removeMarkers <- c(removeMarkers, stats::na.omit(markerExcludeMatch$matched))

# 'Marker Pairs' ("Tregs: FoxP3 CD25") take the spelling of the markers in the
# panel, so every later step can find them exactly
if ("Marker Pairs" %in% colnames(smd)) {
  for (r in which(!is.na(smd[["Marker Pairs"]]))) {
    parts <- strsplit(smd[["Marker Pairs"]][[r]], "\\:\\s*")[[1]]
    if (length(parts) < 2) next
    pairMarkers <- strsplit(trimws(parts[[2]]), "\\s+")[[1]]
    pairMatch <- MARMOT::match_names(pairMarkers, useMarkers)
    nameNotes <- c(nameNotes, MARMOT::describe_name_matches(
      pairMatch$notes, paste0("marker in the pair '", parts[[1]], "'"), "your markers"))
    pairMarkers <- dplyr::coalesce(pairMatch$matched, pairMarkers)
    smd[["Marker Pairs"]][[r]] <- paste0(parts[[1]], ": ", paste(pairMarkers, collapse = " "))
  }
}

if (length(nameNotes)) {
  overviewWarnings <- c(overviewWarnings, paste0(
    "::: {.callout-note title='Names lined up'}\n\n",
    "Your files did not all spell or arrange things the same way, so MARMOT lined them up:\n\n",
    paste0("- ", nameNotes, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n:::\n"))
}

# Build panel
panel <- param_df |>
  dplyr::select(fcs_colname = name, marker_name = desc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    antigen       = marker_name,
    marker_class  = ifelse(marker_name %in% names(markerType), markerType[marker_name], "none"),
    use_channel   = marker_name %in% useMarkers
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!marker_name %in% removeMarkers) |>
  dplyr::filter(marker_name %in% useMarkers) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(marker_name, useMarkers))

# Sanity check
missing <- setdiff(useMarkers, panel$marker_name)
if (length(missing)) {
  stop("❌ Markers in metadata not found in FCS: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}

message("⚙️ Preparing cofactors for arcsinh transformation...")

# Base cofactor vector, matched to FCS column names
cf <- setNames(cfToUse, panel$fcs_colname[match(useMarkers, panel$marker_name)])

# Fill in default (5) for other channels
all_channels <- panel$fcs_colname
extra_channels <- setdiff(all_channels, names(cf))
cf[extra_channels] <- 2500 # Default cofactor for unused channels

# Ensure correct order
cf <- cf[match(all_channels, names(cf))]

# Alternative version cf2, named by marker name
cf2 <- setNames(cf[match(panel$fcs_colname, names(cf))], panel$marker_name)
cf2 <- cf2[panel$use_channel]

asinh_transforms <- transformList(
  names(cf),
  lapply(cf, function(cof) arcsinhTransform(a = 0, b = 1 / cof, c = 0))
)
```

```{r analysis_qc_check, include = FALSE, eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}
if (runQC %in% c("FlowAI", "PeacoQC")) {
  sample_sizes <- originalCellCounts
  min_events <- min(sample_sizes)
  small_sample <- names(which.min(sample_sizes))

  if (min_events < 2000) {
    warning("Sample '", small_sample, "' has only ", min_events,
            " events. Skipping QC.")
    qc_skip_reason <- paste0(
      "Sample **", small_sample, "** has only **", min_events,
      "** events — too few for any automated QC tool (minimum ~2,000). ",
      "QC has been **skipped** for this run. ",
      "With so few events, automated QC is tenuous at best — ",
      "consider acquiring more events or excluding very small samples.")
    runQC <- "None"
    useQC <- FALSE

  } else if (runQC == "PeacoQC" && min_events < 5000) {
    warning("Sample '", small_sample, "' has only ", min_events,
            " events. Skipping PeacoQC.")
    qc_skip_reason <- paste0(
      "Sample **", small_sample, "** has only **", min_events,
      "** events — PeacoQC requires ~5,000+ events per sample for its ",
      "MAD outlier detection. QC has been **skipped** for this run. ",
      "With so few events, automated QC is tenuous at best. ",
      "To run QC on this dataset, try **FlowAI** (works with ~2,000+ events), ",
      "or set `runQC` to `None` to skip QC entirely.")
    runQC <- "None"
    useQC <- FALSE
  }
}
```

```{r analysis_qc_flowai, results = "asis", include = FALSE, eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

if (runQC == "FlowAI") {

  message("🔍 Starting automated quality control...")

  metricsQC <- "FR_FS"

  qc_dir <- file.path(fp, "resultsQC_flowAI")
  expected_qc_files <- gsub("\\.fcs$", "_QC.fcs", md$file_name)
  # QC'd files on disk are reused only if they were made from exactly these FCS
  # files with exactly these QC settings (see ?MARMOT::qc_cache_stamp).
  qc_stamp <- MARMOT::qc_cache_stamp(fcs_files, "FlowAI", list(remove_from = metricsQC))
  qc_present <- dir.exists(qc_dir) &&
    all(expected_qc_files %in% list.files(qc_dir, pattern = "_QC\\.fcs", ignore.case = TRUE)) &&
    MARMOT::qc_cache_is_current(qc_dir, qc_stamp)
  qcWasReused <- qc_present

  if (qc_present) {
    message("📁 QC files found on disk — skipping recomputation.")
  } else {
    message("⚙️  Running FlowAI per-file at full resolution...")
    # Start from an empty folder, so nothing from an earlier run is mixed in
    unlink(qc_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    dir.create(qc_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

    for (i in seq_along(fcs_files)) {
      message(sprintf("  [%d/%d] %s (%s cells)",
                      i, length(fcs_files), basename(fcs_files[i]),
                      format(originalCellCounts[i], big.mark = ",")))
      ff <- flowCore::read.FCS(fcs_files[i], transformation = FALSE,
                                truncate_max_range = FALSE) |>
        MARMOT::lineup_fcs_frame(fcsLineup, basename(fcs_files[i]))
      flow_auto_qc(
        fcsfiles       = ff,
        folder_results = qc_dir,
        remove_from    = metricsQC
      )
      # FlowAI decides which cells to remove, but its own "high quality" file
      # is not used: it clips bright values at the channel's declared range
      # and rewrites Time. FlowAI's `_QC.fcs` holds every event, in order, with
      # a flag (below 10,000 = keep). The kept cells are taken from the
      # original file with that flag, and numbered so each can be traced back.
      flagged <- flowCore::read.FCS(
        file.path(qc_dir, sub("\\.fcs$", "_QC.fcs", basename(fcs_files[i]), ignore.case = TRUE)),
        transformation = FALSE, truncate_max_range = FALSE)
      keep <- flowCore::exprs(flagged)[, paste0("remove_from_", metricsQC)] < 10000
      stopifnot(length(keep) == nrow(ff))
      flowCore::write.FCS(MARMOT::add_event_numbers(ff)[keep, ],
                          file.path(qc_dir, sub("\\.fcs$", "_QC_highQ.fcs", basename(fcs_files[i]), ignore.case = TRUE)))
      rm(ff, flagged, keep); invisible(gc())
    }
    MARMOT::qc_cache_write_stamp(qc_dir, qc_stamp)
  }

  # Load and annotate QC summary table
  fcsFilesQC <- list.files(qc_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "_QC_highQ\\.fcs", ignore.case = TRUE)
  fcsFilesQC <- fcsFilesQC[grep(paste(gsub("\\.fcs", "", md$file_name), collapse = "|"), fcsFilesQC, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  fcsNamesQC <- sub("_QC_highQ\\.fcs$", "", basename(fcsFilesQC))

  QCmini <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(qc_dir, "QCmini.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::distinct(`Name file`, .keep_all = TRUE)
  QCmini <- QCmini[grep(paste0(fcsNamesQC, collapse = "|"), QCmini$`Name file`), ]

  qc_names_clean <- sub("_QC_highQ|\\.fcs", "", QCmini$`Name file`)
  md_names_clean <- sub("\\.fcs$", "", md$file_name)
  QCmini$`Sample Name` <- md$sample_id[match(qc_names_clean, md_names_clean)]
  QCmini <- QCmini[gtools::mixedorder(QCmini$`Name file`), ]

  message("🎉 FlowAI QC complete.")
}
```

```{r analysis_qc_peacoqc, results = "asis", include = FALSE, eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}
if (runQC == "PeacoQC") {

  message("🔍 Starting automated quality control with PeacoQC...🦚")

  qc_dir <- file.path(fp, "resultsQC_peacoQC")

  # Determine fluorescence channels from one frame's metadata
  all_channels <- param_df$name
  fluor_channels <- all_channels[!grepl("^(FSC|SSC|Time)", all_channels, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  fluor_channels <- fluor_channels[!grepl("(Width|Height|Trigger)", fluor_channels, ignore.case = TRUE)]

  # QC'd files on disk are reused only if they were made from exactly these FCS
  # files with exactly these QC settings (see ?MARMOT::qc_cache_stamp). PeacoQC
  # judges the arcsinh-transformed data, so the cofactors are QC settings too.
  qc_stamp <- MARMOT::qc_cache_stamp(fcs_files, "PeacoQC", list(
    channels = fluor_channels,
    cofactors = as.list(cf[fluor_channels]),
    determine_good_cells = "all"
  ))
  qc_present <- dir.exists(qc_dir) && {
    expected_qc_files <- gsub("\\.fcs$", "_QC.fcs", md$file_name)
    actual_qc_paths <- list.files(qc_dir, pattern = "_QC\\.fcs$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
    all(expected_qc_files %in% basename(actual_qc_paths))
  } && MARMOT::qc_cache_is_current(qc_dir, qc_stamp)
  qcWasReused <- qc_present

  if (qc_present) {
    message("📁 QC files found on disk — skipping recomputation.")
  } else {
    message("⚙️  Running PeacoQC per-file at full resolution...")

    # Start from an empty folder, so nothing from an earlier run is mixed in
    unlink(qc_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    dir.create(qc_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

    message("🔬 Using channels for QC: ", paste(fluor_channels, collapse = ", "))
    message("🚫 Excluded channels: ", paste(setdiff(all_channels, fluor_channels), collapse = ", "))

    for (i in seq_along(fcs_files)) {
      fcs_name <- fcs_names[i]
      message(sprintf("  [%d/%d] %s (%s cells)",
                      i, length(fcs_files), fcs_name,
                      format(originalCellCounts[i], big.mark = ",")))
      ff <- flowCore::read.FCS(fcs_files[i], transformation = FALSE,
                                truncate_max_range = FALSE) |>
        MARMOT::lineup_fcs_frame(fcsLineup, basename(fcs_files[i]))
      ff_t <- flowCore::transform(ff, asinh_transforms)

      # PeacoQC judges the transformed data, but the cells it keeps are saved
      # untransformed (as FlowAI's are), so no cofactor is baked into the files.
      # They are numbered first, so each can be traced back to the original file.
      peaco <- PeacoQC::PeacoQC(
        ff = ff_t, channels = fluor_channels,
        plot = TRUE, save_fcs = FALSE,
        output_directory = qc_dir, name_directory = fcs_name,
        report = TRUE, determine_good_cells = "all"
      )
      qc_fcs_dir <- file.path(qc_dir, fcs_name, "fcs_files")
      dir.create(qc_fcs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
      flowCore::write.FCS(MARMOT::add_event_numbers(ff)[peaco$GoodCells, ],
                          file.path(qc_fcs_dir, sub("\\.fcs$", "_QC.fcs", fcs_name, ignore.case = TRUE)))
      rm(ff, ff_t, peaco); invisible(gc())
    }

    # Generate combined QC summary table
    qc_files <- list.files(path = qc_dir, pattern = "report\\.txt", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
    QCmini <- readr::read_tsv(qc_files[[1]], show_col_types = FALSE)
    if (length(qc_files) > 1) {
      for (j in 2:length(qc_files)) {
        xx <- readr::read_tsv(qc_files[[j]], show_col_types = FALSE)
        QCmini[j, ] <- xx[1, ]
      }
    }
    readr::write_tsv(QCmini, file.path(qc_dir, "QCmini.txt"))
    MARMOT::qc_cache_write_stamp(qc_dir, qc_stamp)
    message("✅ PeacoQC processing complete.")
  }

  # Load QC summary table
  fcsFilesQC <- list.files(qc_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "_QC\\.fcs$", recursive = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  fcsFilesQC <- fcsFilesQC[grep(paste(md$file_name, collapse = "|"), fcsFilesQC, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  fcsNamesQC <- sub("_QC\\.fcs$", "", basename(fcsFilesQC))

  QCmini <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(qc_dir, "QCmini.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  QCmini <- QCmini[grep(paste0(fcsNamesQC, collapse = "|"), QCmini$Filename), ]

  message("🎉 PeacoQC QC complete.")
}
```

```{r analysis_fcs_load, include = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

message("📥 Loading FCS data into memory...")

# Helper: read one FCS file and apply RAM cap if needed.
# Original files have their events numbered here, before any are dropped, so
# each cell can be traced back. QC'd files were numbered when QC wrote them.
read_and_cap <- function(f, number_events = FALSE) {
  ff <- flowCore::read.FCS(f, transformation = FALSE, truncate_max_range = FALSE)
  # Original files are lined up here; QC'd files were lined up before QC wrote them
  if (number_events) ff <- MARMOT::lineup_fcs_frame(ff, fcsLineup, basename(f))
  if (number_events) ff <- MARMOT::add_event_numbers(ff)
  if (needs_cap && nrow(ff) > per_sample_cap) {
    set.seed(2)
    ff <- ff[sort(sample(nrow(ff), per_sample_cap)), ]
  }
  ff
}

# Load only the data that will actually be used for analysis
if (useQC && runQC == "FlowAI" && exists("qc_dir") && dir.exists(qc_dir)) {
  # useQC=TRUE, FlowAI: load only QC'd FCS files
  # Each QC'd file is found by the exact name FlowAI's step wrote it under,
  # and takes its File Data name ("S_1" must not pick up "S_10")
  expectedQC <- sub("\\.fcs$", "_QC_highQ.fcs", basename(fcs_files), ignore.case = TRUE)
  fcsFilesQC <- list.files(qc_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "_QC_highQ\\.fcs$", ignore.case = TRUE)
  fcsFilesQC <- fcsFilesQC[basename(fcsFilesQC) %in% expectedQC]

  framesList <- list()
  framesList[["FlowAI"]] <- setNames(
    lapply(fcsFilesQC, read_and_cap),
    fcs_names[match(basename(fcsFilesQC), expectedQC)]
  )
  invisible(lapply(framesList[["FlowAI"]], range, type = "data"))

} else if (useQC && runQC == "PeacoQC" && exists("qc_dir") && dir.exists(qc_dir)) {
  # useQC=TRUE, PeacoQC: load only QC'd FCS files
  # Each QC'd file is found by the exact folder and name PeacoQC's step wrote
  # it under, and takes its File Data name ("S_1" must not pick up "S_10")
  expectedQC <- file.path(fcs_names, "fcs_files", sub("\\.fcs$", "_QC.fcs", fcs_names, ignore.case = TRUE))
  fcsFilesQC <- list.files(qc_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "_QC\\.fcs$", recursive = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  qcRelative <- file.path(basename(dirname(dirname(fcsFilesQC))), "fcs_files", basename(fcsFilesQC))
  fcsFilesQC <- fcsFilesQC[qcRelative %in% expectedQC]

  framesList <- list()
  framesList[["PeacoQC"]] <- setNames(
    lapply(fcsFilesQC, read_and_cap),
    fcs_names[match(qcRelative[qcRelative %in% expectedQC], expectedQC)]
  )
  invisible(lapply(framesList[["PeacoQC"]], range, type = "data"))

} else {
  # useQC=FALSE or no QC: load raw files → build Transformed
  frames <- setNames(lapply(fcs_files, read_and_cap, number_events = TRUE), fcs_names)
  if (!is.null(excludeTheseSamples)) {
    keep_samples <- md$file_name[!md$sample_id %in% excludeTheseSamples]
    frames <- frames[keep_samples]
  }
  framesList <- list("Untransformed" = frames)
  rm(frames)
}

invisible(gc())

effective_cells <- sum(sapply(framesList[[1]], nrow))
message(sprintf("📊 Loaded %s cells (%.1f GB estimated)",
                format(effective_cells, big.mark = ","),
                effective_cells * bytes_per_cell / 1024^3))

# ── Diagnostic: FCS load shape (no sample labels) ─────────────────────────
MARMOT::run_log_record(log_path, "fcs_load", list(
  n_cells_total_raw   = as.integer(total_cells_raw),
  n_cells_total_used  = as.integer(effective_cells),
  cells_per_sample    = as.integer(unname(sapply(framesList[[1]], nrow))),
  n_params            = as.integer(n_params),
  ram_cap_applied     = isTRUE(needs_cap),
  per_sample_cap      = as.integer(per_sample_cap),
  sys_ram_gb_detected = if (is.finite(sys_ram_gb)) sys_ram_gb else NA_real_
))
MARMOT::run_log_checkpoint(log_path, "analysis_fcs_load")
```

```{r analysis_flowsets, include = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}
message("📦 Converting frame lists into flowSets...")

# Convert to flowSet and set $CYT keyword to "FACS"
# Also enforce sampleNames from the list names: read.FCS() embeds the on-disk
# filename (e.g. "Sample_001_QC.fcs") as the frame identifier, which would
# cause CATALYST::prepData() to fail matching against md$file_name.
fsList <- purrr::imap(framesList, function(sample_list, name) {
  fs <- as(sample_list, "flowSet")
  sampleNames(fs) <- names(sample_list)
  for (j in seq_along(fs)) {
    keyword(fs[[j]])[["$CYT"]] <- "FACS"
  }
  fs
})
```

```{r analysis_cofactor_histograms, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

message("📉 Generating cofactor histograms for visualising transformations...")

cofactorsToTry <- c(5, 50, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000, 15000)

# Aggressively downsample (use whatever data was loaded — raw or QC'd).
# QC'd data are already arcsinh-transformed by this point; raw data are not.
histosAlreadyTransformed <- !"Untransformed" %in% names(framesList)
framesList[["Marker Histos"]] <- lapply(framesList[[1]], function(fcs) {
  if (nrow(fcs) > 1000) {
    set.seed(2)
    fcs[sample(nrow(fcs), 1000), ]
  } else {
    fcs
  }
})

# Function to strip data from ggplot object
minify_plot_data <- function(p, colname, group_col = "condition") {
  # Keep only the columns needed for plotting (x and fill/colour)
  vars_needed <- unique(c(colname, group_col))
  p$data <- p$data[, vars_needed, drop = FALSE]
  p
}

# Plot generation without persistent cofactorDFList
cofactorPlotList <- lapply(useMarkers, function(marker) {
  colname <- panel$fcs_colname[panel$marker_name == marker]
  marker_expr <- purrr::map(framesList[["Marker Histos"]], ~ exprs(.x)[, colname])
  
  # Flat vector of expression values
  expr_vec <- unlist(marker_expr)
  # Undo the arcsinh on QC'd data, so the histograms start from raw values
  if (histosAlreadyTransformed) expr_vec <- sinh(expr_vec) * cf[[colname]]
  sample_vec <- rep(names(marker_expr), times = purrr::map_int(marker_expr, length))
  cond_vec <- md$condition[match(gsub("\\.fcs$", "", sample_vec), gsub("\\.fcs$", "", md$file_name))]

  # Build only what's needed: wide format DF with just transformed values + condition
  df <- tibble::tibble(
    condition = cond_vec,
    pretransform = expr_vec
  )

  # Transform in-place
  transformed_cols <- purrr::map(cofactorsToTry, function(cof) {
    tibble::tibble(!!paste0("Cofactor_", cof) := asinh(expr_vec / cof))
  }) |> purrr::list_cbind()

  df <- dplyr::bind_cols(df, transformed_cols)

  # Generate plots and strip ggplot data
  plot_names <- c("pretransform", paste0("Cofactor_", cofactorsToTry))
  plot_set <- purrr::map(plot_names, function(colname) {
    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[colname]], fill = condition, colour = condition)) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.1) +
      ggtitle(colname) +
      theme_prism() +
      theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "none") +
      scale_colour_manual(values = coloursList$condition, labels = MARMOT::greek_label) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = coloursList$condition, labels = MARMOT::greek_label) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = mean(df[[colname]], na.rm = TRUE), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red")
    minify_plot_data(p, colname)
  })

  setNames(plot_set, plot_names)
})

names(cofactorPlotList) <- useMarkers
```

```{r analysis_cell_object, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}
if (useQC) {
  message("✅ Using QC-filtered data for downstream analysis.")
  fsToUse <- fsList[[runQC]]
} else {
  fsToUse <- fsList[["Transformed"]]
}

if (!is.null(downsampleTo)) {
  message("🔽 Downsampling to ", downsampleTo, " cells per sample.")
  fsToUse <- fsApply(fsToUse, function(x) {
    set.seed(2)
    n_events <- nrow(x)
    sample_size <- min(downsampleTo, n_events)
    sampled_indices <- sample(n_events, sample_size)
    x[sampled_indices, ]
  })
}

message("📦 Creating SingleCellExperiment objects with CATALYST::prepData...")

sce <- CATALYST::prepData(
  x = fsToUse,
  panel = panel,
  md = md,
  features = panel$fcs_colname,
  transform = FALSE,
  md_cols = list(factors = conditions)
)
# Record which event of its original FCS file each cell is
sce <- MARMOT::record_event_numbers(sce, fsToUse, md)
# exprs and exprsTransformed are identical to counts at this stage (transformation
# was applied at the flowFrame level, before prepData).  Share the same matrix
# object to avoid tripling memory — R's copy-on-modify means no duplication until
# one is actually written to (which the pipeline does not do).
.shared_mat <- assay(sce, "counts")
assay(sce, "exprs") <- .shared_mat
assay(sce, "exprsTransformed") <- .shared_mat
rm(.shared_mat)

# 99% quantile normalisation
message("📐 Applying quantile normalisation...")

exprs_mat <- assay(sce, "exprs")
qs <- matrixStats::rowQuantiles(exprs_mat, probs = c(0.01, 0.99))
norm_exprs <- sweep(exprs_mat, 1, qs[, 1], "-")
norm_exprs <- sweep(norm_exprs, 1, qs[, 2] - qs[, 1], "/")
norm_exprs[norm_exprs < 0 | is.na(norm_exprs)] <- 0
norm_exprs[norm_exprs > 1] <- 1

assay(sce, "exprsQuantNorm") <- norm_exprs

# Also include a scaled version
scale.coef <- matrixStats::rowQuantiles(exprs_mat, probs = c(0.01, 0.99))
assay(sce, "norm") <- t(scale(t(exprs_mat), center = scale.coef[, 1], scale = scale.coef[, 2] - scale.coef[, 1]))

# Free the frames and intermediates: everything needed from here on is in
# `sce`. The frames are not saved; the results record each cell's event
# number instead, so cells can be traced back to the original FCS files.
rm(exprs_mat, norm_exprs, qs, scale.coef)
if (exists("framesList")) rm(framesList)
if (exists("fsList")) rm(fsList)
if (exists("fsToUse")) rm(fsToUse)
invisible(gc())
```

```{r analysis_batch_correction, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

# What clustering works on: the cells' values for the clustering markers.
clusterInput <- t(assay(sce, exprsToUse)[featuresToCluster, ])

# With batchColumn set, Harmony moves each cell within a PCA of those markers
# so that the batches overlap, and clustering and the embeddings use the
# corrected positions. Marker values are never changed: every heatmap, marker
# plot and DS test uses the measured values, and the batch is allowed for in
# the DA/DS models instead (see analysis_da_ds and the Batch correction tab).
if (useBatch) {
  message("🧪 Correcting for batch ('", batchColumn, "') with Harmony...")
  pcsUncorrected <- prcomp(clusterInput, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)$x   # every PC: a rotation, nothing lost
  set.seed(2)                                                              # Harmony repeats exactly only with a seed here
  clusterInput <- harmony::RunHarmony(pcsUncorrected, meta_data = data.frame(batch = sce[[batchColumn]]),
                                      vars_use = "batch", verbose = FALSE)
  reducedDim(sce, "PCA_uncorrected") <- pcsUncorrected
  reducedDim(sce, "PCA_harmony") <- clusterInput
}
```

```{r analysis_clustering_graph, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

if (clusteringMethodToUse %in% c("MfastPG", "Mphenograph", "Rphenograph")) {
  message("🧠 Running clustering using ", clusteringMethodToUse, "...")

  # Expression matrix for clustering
  es <- clusterInput   # the clustering markers, batch-corrected when batchColumn is set

  # Mphenograph and Rphenograph search for neighbours exactly, so a cell's k
  # nearest neighbours are the first k of its neighbours at the largest k.
  # Search once, at the largest k, and let every k take its share: the
  # clusters are exactly the same, and the slowest step runs only once.
  if (clusteringMethodToUse %in% c("Mphenograph", "Rphenograph")) {
    message("  ▸ Finding the ", max(kValuesIWant), " nearest neighbours of each cell, once for every k...")
    nnShared <- MARMOT::nearest_neighbours(es, k = max(kValuesIWant) + 1)
  }

  cluster_fn <- function(k) {
    set.seed(2)
    if (clusteringMethodToUse == "MfastPG") {
      clusters <- MARMOT::MfastPG(data = es, k = k, seed = 2, verbose = TRUE)
    } else if (clusteringMethodToUse == "Mphenograph") {
      clusters <- MARMOT::Mphenograph(data = es, k = k, seed = 2, verbose = TRUE, nn_idx = nnShared)
    } else if (clusteringMethodToUse == "Rphenograph") {
      clusters <- Rphenograph::Rphenograph(data = es, k = k,
                                           knn_fun = function(data, kk) nnShared[, seq_len(kk)])
    }
    ids <- factor(as.character(igraph::membership(clusters[[2]])))
    ids <- factor(ids, levels = gtools::mixedsort(levels(ids)))
    list(kids = ids, clusters = clusters)
  }

  kList <- setNames(lapply(kValuesIWant, cluster_fn), paste0("k", kValuesIWant))

  # Store all clusterings in SCE object
  for (k in names(kList)) {
    sce[[k]] <- kList[[k]]$kids
  }

  # Select default cluster to use
  selected_k <- paste0("k", knn)
  sce$cluster_id <- sce[[selected_k]]
  
  metadata(sce)$cluster_codes <- setNames(
    data.frame(factor(levels(sce[[selected_k]]))), clusteringMethodToUse
  )
```

```{r analysis_clustering_parc, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

if (clusteringMethodToUse == "PARC") {
  if (!MARMOT:::use_marmot_python()) {
    message("Python PARC unavailable -- falling back to Mparc (R).")
    clusteringMethodToUse <- "Mparc"
  } else {
  message("🐍 Running PARC clustering...")

  set.seed(2)
  esPARC <- clusterInput   # batch-corrected when batchColumn is set

  # Run PARC in an isolated Python subprocess. Same process as R would collide
  # libomp runtimes (R's data.table libomp vs conda's annoy/hnswlib libomp on
  # macOS arm64) and segfault. The subprocess writes/reads raw float64 via
  # temp files so reticulate is bypassed entirely.
  parcClustList <- setNames(lapply(kValuesIWant, function(k) {
    labels <- MARMOT:::run_parc_subprocess(
      esPARC, knn = k, num_threads = nCores
    )
    as.integer(labels)
  }), paste0("p", kValuesIWant))

  for (k in kValuesIWant) {
    cluster_labels <- factor(as.character(parcClustList[[paste0("p", k)]] + 1))
    cluster_labels <- factor(cluster_labels, levels = gtools::mixedsort(levels(cluster_labels)))
    sce[[paste0("p", k)]] <- cluster_labels
  }

  chosen_k <- paste0("p", knn)
  sce$cluster_id <- sce[[chosen_k]]
  metadata(sce)$cluster_codes <- setNames(
    data.frame(factor(levels(sce[[chosen_k]]))), clusteringMethodToUse
  )
  kids <- sce[[paste0("p", knn)]]
  numbersOfClusters <- gtools::mixedsort(levels(kids))
  }
}
```

```{r analysis_dim_reduction, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

message("📉 Running dimensionality reduction: ", dimRedMethodToUse)

# Fix seed so DR is identical regardless of which clustering method ran before this
set.seed(2)

# Select features for DR
if (homogeneousPanel) {
  featuresToUmap <- panel$marker_name
} else if (!is.null(featureType) && markersToDimRedBy == "type") {
  featuresToUmap <- panel$marker_name[panel$marker_class == "type"]
} else if (!is.null(featureType) && markersToDimRedBy == "state") {
  featuresToUmap <- panel$marker_name[panel$marker_class == "state"]
} else {
  featuresToUmap <- panel$marker_name
}

n_cells_dr <- ncol(sce)

# Always run PCA first (needed for pacmap, helpful for others)
message("  ▸ PCA on ", n_cells_dr, " cells × ", length(featuresToUmap), " features...")
t0 <- Sys.time()
sce <- runDR(x = sce, dr = "PCA", features = featuresToUmap, assay = exprsToUse)
message("    done (", format(round(Sys.time() - t0, 1)), ")")

# With batchColumn set, the embeddings are drawn from Harmony-corrected
# positions too: the clustering's, when the markers are the same, otherwise a
# Harmony run of their own on the embedding markers.
if (useBatch) {
  drInput <- if (setequal(featuresToUmap, featuresToCluster)) clusterInput else {
    pcsDR <- prcomp(t(assay(sce, exprsToUse)[featuresToUmap, ]), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)$x
    set.seed(2)
    harmony::RunHarmony(pcsDR, meta_data = data.frame(batch = sce[[batchColumn]]), vars_use = "batch", verbose = FALSE)
  }
  reducedDim(sce, "PCA_harmony_dr") <- drInput
  set.seed(2)
}

# PaCMAP — runs in an isolated Python subprocess (see R/run_python_dr.R).
# In-process reticulate collides libomp runtimes with R's data.table on
# macOS arm64 and segfaults during ANNOY's NN search. Falls back to Mpacmap
# (pure R) if the p4r conda env is missing or the subprocess errors.
if (dimRedMethodToUse == "pacmap") {
  es <- if (useBatch) as.matrix(drInput) else as.matrix(t(assay(sce, exprsToUse)[featuresToUmap, ]))
  embedding <- MARMOT:::run_pacmap_subprocess(es, apply_pca = FALSE, random_state = 2L, verbose = TRUE)
  if (is.null(embedding)) {
    message("PaCMAP failed -- falling back to Mpacmap (R).")
    dimRedMethodToUse <- "Mpacmap"
  } else {
    colnames(embedding) <- c("x", "y")
    reducedDim(sce, dimRedMethodToUse) <- embedding
  }
}

# Mpacmap (pure R) — also used as fallback when Python PaCMAP is unavailable
if (dimRedMethodToUse == "Mpacmap") {
  message("Running Mpacmap (R)...")
  es <- if (useBatch) as.data.frame(drInput) else as.data.frame(t(assay(sce, exprsToUse)[featuresToUmap, ]))
  # Put the random-number stream back afterwards, so the UMAP and tSNE below
  # come out the same whichever method was chosen
  seedBeforeMpacmap <- .Random.seed
  embedding <- Mpacmap(as.matrix(es), apply_pca = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)
  assign(".Random.seed", seedBeforeMpacmap, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  colnames(embedding) <- c("x", "y")
  reducedDim(sce, "Mpacmap") <- embedding
}

# Native DRs (from the corrected positions when batchColumn is set)
drFrom <- if (useBatch) "PCA_harmony_dr" else NULL
sce <- runDR(x = sce, dr = "UMAP", features = featuresToUmap, assay = exprsToUse, dimred = drFrom)
sce <- runDR(x = sce, dr = "TSNE", features = featuresToUmap, assay = exprsToUse, dimred = drFrom, num_threads = nCores)

# ... and an uncorrected UMAP beside it, so the correction can be judged
if (useBatch) {
  set.seed(2)
  reducedDim(sce, "UMAP_uncorrected") <- reducedDim(
    runDR(x = sce, dr = "UMAP", features = featuresToUmap, assay = exprsToUse), "UMAP")
}
```

```{r, label = "analysis_scgate_run", include = FALSE}
if (is.null(RDataFolder) && runScGate) {
  if (requireNamespace("scGate", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("UCell", quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("Running scGate on marker pairs...")
    mp <- parse_marker_pairs(smd)

    if (is.null(mp) || length(mp$models) == 0) {
      warning("No marker pairs defined in metadata — skipping scGate.")
      runScGate <- FALSE
    } else {
      models <- mp$models
      gatePassed <- list()   # per gate: which cells passed it
      gateScore  <- list()   # per gate: every cell's score for it

    for (x in names(models)) {
      if (!models[[x]][[1]] %in% rownames(scData)) {
        # Seurat writes underscores as hyphens; match as everywhere else
        hit <- stats::na.omit(MARMOT::match_names(models[[x]][[1]], rownames(scData))$matched)
        if (length(hit) == 0) {
          warning("No marker match for '", models[[x]][[1]], "' in model '", x, "' — skipping model.")
          next
        }
        models[[x]][[1]] <- hit[[1]]
      }
      if (!models[[x]][[2]] %in% rownames(scData)) {
        # Seurat writes underscores as hyphens; match as everywhere else
        hit <- stats::na.omit(MARMOT::match_names(models[[x]][[2]], rownames(scData))$matched)
        if (length(hit) == 0) {
          warning("No marker match for '", models[[x]][[2]], "' in model '", x, "' — skipping model.")
          next
        }
        models[[x]][[2]] <- hit[[1]]
      }
      model <- scGate::gating_model(name = x, signature = c(models[[x]][[1]], models[[x]][[2]]))
      scoresBefore <- grep("UCell$", colnames(scData@meta.data), value = TRUE)
      scData <- scGate::scGate(data = scData, model = model, pos.thr = 0.65)
      # scGate marks the cells that pass a gate "Pure" in is.pure
      passed <- scData$is.pure %in% "Pure"
      y <- gsub("[ -]", "", x)
      scData[[paste0("is_", y)]] <- ifelse(passed, x, NA_character_)
      # This gate's score for every cell (the UCell column scGate just added)
      newScore <- setdiff(grep("UCell$", colnames(scData@meta.data), value = TRUE), scoresBefore)
      gatePassed[[x]] <- passed
      gateScore[[x]] <- if (length(newScore)) scData@meta.data[[newScore[1]]] else as.numeric(passed)
    }

    # Gated_Cells: of the gates a cell passed, the one it scores highest on;
    # cells that passed no gate are "Negative"
    if (length(gatePassed) > 0) {
      passedM <- do.call(cbind, gatePassed)
      scoreM <- do.call(cbind, gateScore)
      scoreM[!passedM] <- -Inf
      scData$Gated_Cells <- ifelse(rowSums(passedM) > 0,
                                   colnames(scoreM)[max.col(scoreM, ties.method = "first")],
                                   "Negative")
    } else {
      scData$Gated_Cells <- "Negative"
    }

    # Transfer scGate results back to SCE
    sce$Gated_Cells <- scData$Gated_Cells
    scgate_cols <- grep("^is_|UCell", colnames(scData@meta.data), value = TRUE)
    for (col in scgate_cols) {
      sce[[col]] <- scData@meta.data[[col]]
    }

    # Add gate colours
    gate_colours <- setup_scgate_colours(unique(scData$Gated_Cells), names(models), catalystCols)
    for (nm in names(gate_colours)) coloursList[[nm]] <- gate_colours[[nm]]
    } # end: mp non-NULL branch
  } else {
    warning("scGate and/or UCell are not installed — skipping scGate analysis.")
    runScGate <- FALSE
  }
}
```

```{r analysis_plotting_tables, results = "hide", eval = is.null(RDataFolder)}

message("🧭 Preparing dimensionality reduction dataframes for all methods...")

# Get available DR methods with 2D coords
dr_methods <- reducedDimNames(sce)
valid_methods <- dr_methods[sapply(dr_methods, function(m) ncol(reducedDim(sce, m)) >= 2)]
# The PCA positions behind batch correction are not embeddings to draw
valid_methods <- setdiff(valid_methods, c("PCA_uncorrected", "PCA_harmony", "PCA_harmony_dr"))

# Function to build one DR dataframe
build_dr_df <- function(method) {
  coords <- reducedDim(sce, method)[, 1:2]
  colnames(coords) <- c("x", "y")
  df <- data.frame(
    colData(sce),
    sce_idx = seq_len(ncol(sce)),
    coords,
    DRMethod = method,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  
  # Add cluster annotations
  if (!is.null(metadata(sce)$cluster_codes)) {
    df <- dplyr::left_join(df, cluster_codes(sce), by = c("cluster_id" = clusteringMethodToUse))
  }
  df[[clusteringMethodToUse]] <- df$cluster_id

  # Add quantile-normalised expression
  qn <- t(assay(sce, "exprsQuantNorm"))
  df <- dplyr::bind_cols(df, as.data.frame(qn))
  
  # Drop only rows with missing DR coordinates (not all NAs — scGate is_* columns
  # have NA for negative cells and must be preserved)
  df <- df[!is.na(df$x) & !is.na(df$y), , drop = FALSE]
  
  return(df)
}

# Build full DR list
umapDFList <- lapply(valid_methods, build_dr_df)
names(umapDFList) <- valid_methods

# Optionally downsample per condition
if (!is.null(drCellPerCondition)) {
  set.seed(2)
  for (method in valid_methods) {
    df <- umapDFList[[method]]
    down_df <- df |>
      dplyr::group_by(sample_id) |>
      dplyr::group_modify(~ {
        cond <- unique(md$condition[md$sample_id == .y$sample_id])
        target_n <- as.numeric(drCellPerCondition[as.character(cond)])
        if (nrow(.x) > target_n) .x[sample(nrow(.x), target_n), ] else .x
      }) |>
      dplyr::ungroup()
    down_df <- droplevels(down_df)
    umapDFList[[paste0("Downsampled.", method)]] <- down_df
  }
}

# Create label vectors for each DR method
labsList <- lapply(valid_methods, function(method) {
  source_group <- if (!is.null(drCellPerCondition)) paste0("Downsampled.", method) else method
  df <- umapDFList[[source_group]]
  labs <- df |>
    dplyr::group_by(condition) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(label = paste0(condition, "\n n = ", n)) |>
    tibble::deframe()
  names(labs) <- levels(factor(df$condition))
  return(labs)
})
names(labsList) <- valid_methods

umapDFList$All <- umapDFList[[dimRedMethodToUse]]
umapDFList$Downsampled <- umapDFList[[paste0("Downsampled.", dimRedMethodToUse)]]
```
